claims.text: The Mercedes A‑Class (W177) uses Mercedes’ MBUX layout with twin 10.25‑inch displays and can be controlled via the central touchscreen, touch‑sensitive steering controls, a centre‑console touchpad and voice commands.
Mercedes’ MBUX introduced a ‘zero layer’ home screen to surface major functions on the home page (intended to reduce menu dives), but reviewers note some shortcut buttons are small and fiddly.
claims.about: MBUX zero layer and distraction mitigation

claims.text: Auto Express’ hands‑on touchscreen tests and reviewer comments for MBUX found testers sometimes ‘concentrat[ed] on the screen a bit more than was ideal’ and recorded longer distracted‑task times for some operations, indicating touchscreen interactions increase in‑drive distraction compared with tactile controls.

Reviewers of the BMW 1 Series F70 (2024/2025) report BMW removed the centre rotary iDrive controller and relocated climate and many other controls to the touchscreen, increasing driver reliance on the display.

A CompleteCar review of the BMW 120 (F70) concluded that although BMW keeps temperature and seat‑heating controls visible on the screen, using the touchscreen for climate/audio is ‘still more distracting than a button or even a rotary dial.’
claims.about: BMW touchscreen vs physical controls distraction

claims.text: Evo’s A‑Class review reports Mercedes’ voice assistant is ‘among the best’ tested and that voice control is ‘as a means of distraction‑free control of infotainment, better than any touchscreen,’ offering a non‑touch mitigation for touchscreen distraction.
claims.about: Voice control as distraction mitigation in A‑Class

claims.text: Mercedes’ official owner/manual pages for the 2025 A‑Class describe operation of MBUX via touchscreen, touch control on the steering wheel and voice control, confirming multiple input methods are provided in EU/European market documentation.
claims.about: Official MBUX operating methods (A‑Class owner manual)
